intended_object: The normal bundle of a C¹ immersion f : M → V into a finite-dimensional real inner product space, viewed as a topological fibre bundle with model fibre F of dimension dim V − dim M. Its fibre over x is the orthogonal complement of the image of df_x, and its total space has the subspace topology from M × V (as in Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, the construction before Thm 6.24). This is taken from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition builds the `FiberBundle F (fun x => normalSubspace I f x)` structure. Here `normalSubspace I f x` is `(range (mfderiv f x))ᗮ`, which is the Euclidean normal space at x. The topology on the total space is induced from M × V by the instance `instTopologicalSpaceTotalSpaceNormalSubspace`, as the docstring says.

The atlas consists of the local trivializations `normalBundleTrivialization`, one centred at each point x₀. Each sends a normal vector at x to its orthogonal projection onto the normal space at x₀, then identifies that space with F by a fixed linear isomorphism. Lee uses the same projection for local frames. Every point lies in the base set of its own trivialization, and the proof shows the fibre-inclusion maps are inducing. The model fibre F only has to have the right dimension, which `hdim` guarantees, and that is the usual freedom in choosing a model fibre.

The hypotheses are the natural ones for this construction:
- f is C¹, so the normal spaces vary continuously.
- df_x is injective everywhere, so f is an immersion.
- The manifold is boundaryless and finite-dimensional.
- V is an inner product space, which is needed to take orthogonal complements.

Mathlib has no normal bundle, neither the Euclidean one nor the general quotient TV|_M / TM, so it offers no broader notion this should have used. The definition matches the standard Euclidean normal bundle as a fibre bundle.
